options: Microsoft's cloud compute platform, the same thing as Azure
A standalone software delivery platform that can build and ship apps to any cloud, including non-Azure targets
A single service for running container builds only
A certification exam for DevOps engineers
questions.explain: Azure DevOps is a separate delivery platform from the Azure cloud itself. A team can use it to ship an app that runs on AWS, on-premises, or anywhere else.

questions.q: Which Azure DevOps service handles build (CI) and release (CD) automation?
options: Boards
Test Plans
Pipelines
Artifacts
questions.explain: Pipelines is the service dedicated to build and release automation — the focus of this entire chapter.

questions.q: How is an Azure DevOps organization related to a project?
options: A project contains one or more organizations
An organization contains one or more projects
They are the same thing, just different names
Organizations and projects are unrelated containers
questions.explain: An organization is the top-level container, typically one per company, and it holds one or more projects — like Northbridge Retail's storefront project.

questions.q: Why does this course use YAML pipelines instead of the Classic designer?
options: YAML pipelines run faster on every agent
The Classic designer has been fully removed from Azure DevOps
YAML pipelines are checked into source control, so they can be reviewed, diffed, and rolled back like application code
YAML pipelines don't support multiple stages
questions.explain: A YAML pipeline lives as a version-controlled file in the repo, unlike a Classic pipeline built through the visual designer with no file in source control.

questions.q: Can a team use Azure Pipelines to build code stored in a GitHub repository instead of Azure Repos?
options: No, Azure Pipelines only works with Azure Repos
Yes — pipelines don't care where the source code lives
Only if the GitHub repo is first mirrored manually every day
Only for public open-source repositories
questions.explain: Azure Pipelines can target a GitHub repo just as easily as Azure Repos; plenty of organizations mix and match the five Azure DevOps services rather than using all of them.
